newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-MURDOCH SUPER LEAGUE POISED FOR KICK-OFF.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-MURDOCH SUPER LEAGUE POISED FOR KICK-OFF.

text.p: Media baron Rupert Murdoch was set
to launch his rebel Super League competition in Australia next
year after a stunning legal victory on Friday over rugby
league's established order.
Murdoch was freed to start his breakaway league when
Australia's Federal Court overturned an earlier ruling banning
his competition from kicking off before the year 2000.
The legal victory, immediately freeing eight existing clubs
and more than 200 players to defect to Super League, means there
will almost certainly be two rival competitions in Australia
next year and extends Murdoch's control of the sport worldwide.
Murdoch, who already has the backing of Britain and New
Zealand -- the two other major rugby league playing nations --
has fought a bitter power struggle with the Australian Rugby
League (ARL) for almost two years.
"The situation now is that it looks as though there is going
to be two competitions," ARL chairman Ken Arthurson told
reporters outside court, adding that the ARL was considering a
further appeal to a higher court in Australia.
"I've had better days than today," he added.
Murdoch's News Ltd has invested A$270 million (US$213
million) in Super League, securing the loyalty of eight existing
Australian clubs and more than 200 players.
But he was barred from launching Super League in March this
year after an earlier court ruling forced all clubs to honour
loyalty agreements with the ARL.
The federal court on Friday said it found those agreements
were invalid under Australia's anti-monopoly legislation.
Reacting to the decision, Murdoch thanked the players and
clubs who he said had stood by him during the battle.
"They have never lost faith in our belief in what Rugby
League could and should become: a truly international sport
deserving unsurpassed marketing support and promotional
excellence," Murdoch said in a statement.
The eight existing clubs now freed to join Super League are
Brisbane Broncos, Canberra Raiders, Cronulla Sharks, Auckland
Warriors, Western Reds, Sydney Bulldogs, North Queensland and
Penrith.
A host of prominent international players are also
contracted to Super League, including former test scrumhalfs
Ricky Stuart and Allan Langer and backs Laurie Daley and Andrew
Ettingshausen.
Murdoch's Super League plans involved annual playoff matches
between leading clubs in Australia and Europe and regular
internationals involving Australia, New Zealand and Britain.
Although it is now legally free to start its own
competition, the court ruled that Murdoch's News Ltd had to pay
damages to the ARL as it had encouraged clubs to breach their
ARL contracts.
But it limited damages to the 1995 season, during which the
sport enjoyed bumper crowds and no disruption to its programme.
